name: Voiceprint — see which model eats your writing voice
one_liner: Paste three paragraphs you actually wrote and Voiceprint shows four top models rewriting one of them, scores how much of your voice each one destroyed, hands you a copy-paste voice.md that stops it, and posts the week's model-vs-voice leaderboard.
problem: People who write in public — founders posting on X, newsletter writers, devs writing READMEs and PRDs — run drafts through ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini and come back sounding like everyone else. They complain about it constantly (em dashes, "delve", tricolons, the flattened rhythm) and the complaint is now backed by research: LLM revision cut the variance of writing complexity across writers by 21-50% (Nature Human Behaviour, Aug 2026, arXiv:2502.11266). What they do today is either (a) guess, and strip em dashes by superstition, or (b) hand-write a STYLE.md / voice card by asking Claude to describe their style — a private, unmeasured, one-shot ritual. Nobody shows them the actual damage: this model kept your short sentences, that one doubled your clause length and deleted every one of your five favourite words. Without the measurement, the fix is folklore.
target_customer: Writers who post in public and already use LLMs on their drafts: X/indie-hacker founders, Substack and newsletter writers, devrel and technical writers, and the Claude Code / agent crowd who maintain CLAUDE.md and STYLE.md files. They hang out on X, r/WritingWithAI, r/ClaudeCode, Hacker News and in the "anti-slop skills" corner of GitHub. Free tool; no buyer — this is a project, not a business.
why_now: Three things landed in the last few months. (1) The voice-flattening claim stopped being vibes: the Nature Human Behaviour paper (Aug 2026) quantifies the 21-50% variance collapse, so a score has something to stand on. (2) YC's Winter 2027 RFS has "LLMs That Write Well" (Jared Friedman) arguing coding/math reward signals are structurally flattening voice — the exact thesis this tool makes visible per-user (https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs#llms-that-write-well). (3) The cost of running four rewrites fell to nothing: OpenRouter lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 at ~$0.031/M in and $0.27/M out, has a free-model tier (Nemotron 3 Ultra free etc., 20 req/min, 50/day), and supports OAuth PKCE so visitors can bring their own key from a static page (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/auth/oauth). A four-model rewrite bake-off cost real money a year ago; today a paragraph costs a fraction of a cent.
comparables: Idiolect (https://idiolect.app/voice-match) builds a Voice Profile and Voice Card from samples and scores a draft against it — but it measures you against yourself, never names which model wrecked your voice. ScriptGrain's style rewriter (https://scriptgrain.com/us/tools/ai-style-rewriter) does pairwise original-vs-one-rewrite similarity, one at a time, no model attribution. StyleMimic Blind Test (https://stylemimic.com/blind-test) is the closest share mechanic — your writing vs an AI imitation, guess which — but it is a single generated passage, not a model bake-off. Agent-side: unslop (https://github.com/theclaymethod/unslop), avoid-ai-writing (https://github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing) and Claude's built-in Styles all produce voice cards, but require an agent setup and produce no measurement. Benchmarks: TextStyled (https://textstyled.com/benchmarks) and PersonalBench measure style preservation across models, but as research artifacts, not something you can run on your own paragraph; LMArena's creative-writing board is crowd-voted but tests generic quality, not your voice. The gap I found and confirmed: nothing free lets one person paste their own writing, see several named models rewrite it side by side, get an interpretable per-model voice-loss score, and walk away with the fix.
market_note: No market in the paid sense — free and open source. Audience size is the thing: the "AI slop / sounds like ChatGPT" complaint is one of the most repeated writing complaints of 2026 (Wikipedia maintains a "Signs of AI writing" page; Slate covered writers self-censoring em dashes). Estimate, not measured: tens of thousands of people who would try it once, low thousands who would keep a voice.md. Any revenue would be a later hosted "keep my baseline" tier; do not build it.
risks: 1. The score has to feel true. If a writer reads the four rewrites and disagrees with which one "lost" their voice, the whole thing is a party trick. Mitigation: show the receipts, not just a number — the exact sentences that changed, the words of theirs that got deleted, the clause-length graph. Deterministic, inspectable metrics beat an LLM judge here. 2. Key friction. BYO-OpenRouter-key via OAuth is one extra click and will cost some share of visitors; a demo mode with pre-baked samples is mandatory so the value lands before any auth. 3. The adjacent space is crowded (Idiolect, ScriptGrain, dozens of humanizer skills). Differentiation is entirely the per-model attribution and the weekly board; if that framing gets muddled it reads as "another slop checker".
riskiest_assumptions: 1. That a deterministic style-distance score, computed in-browser, is credible enough that writers accept the verdict rather than argue with it. 2. That writers will paste their own writing into a tool at all — the share mechanic dies if people only use the demo samples. 3. That named-model leaderboard results ("Model X destroyed the most voices this week") attract attention rather than takedown-flavoured attention; keep it factual, methodology published.
first_customers: The ten who matter first: people already posting about AI flattening their writing. Reply to the recurring X and r/WritingWithAI threads with their own paragraph run through it. Then the Claude Code / STYLE.md crowd (r/ClaudeCode, the unslop and avoid-ai-writing repo issues) — they already hand-maintain voice files and will take a generated one. Then two or three newsletter writers with an audience who will post their card.
validation_test: Post one card — my own three paragraphs, four models, the voice-loss scores and the two sentences each model wrecked — to X with the link, and drop the same in one Reddit writing thread. Pass: 25+ people paste their own writing within 72 hours and at least 5 post their card unprompted. Fail: people like the screenshot but nobody runs it on themselves, which means the paste barrier is too high and the idea needs a lower-friction input.
build_plan:
Stack: one static page (TypeScript + Vite, no framework needed), deployed to Vercel/Netlify, no backend, no database. Models via OpenRouter: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (~$0.031/M in, $0.27/M out), plus three other named frontier models, all same prompt, all through one endpoint. Auth via OpenRouter OAuth PKCE so each visitor's rewrites bill to their own account; my own key never ships.
Steps: (1) Build the in-browser style metric — sentence-length distribution and variance, clause depth proxy, type-token and hapax ratio, punctuation profile, hedge/intensifier rates, and the writer's top distinctive words; all plain JS, no model needed. Compute a baseline from the three pasted paragraphs. (2) Fan out one paragraph to four models with an identical "tighten this, keep the meaning" prompt — the realistic thing people actually ask. (3) Score each rewrite against the baseline, render the four side by side with the diff highlighted: which of your words died, which sentences doubled in length. (4) Generate voice.md from the baseline — concrete rules with your real numbers and your real words, one copy button, one download. (5) Share card: a PNG of the four model scores plus the single worst sentence each produced, rendered on canvas. (6) Weekly board: results get appended to a public JSON in the repo via a tiny form-to-GitHub action (or, simplest, I append the aggregate myself each Monday) — "models ranked by average voice loss this week", refreshed every Monday, so there's a reason to come back.
Cut: no accounts, no stored text (everything stays in the browser, say so loudly), no LLM-as-judge scoring, no multi-document upload, no Chrome extension, no humanizer/rewrite-it-for-me button. The tool diagnoses and hands you the fix; it does not become another writing assistant.
launch_post:
Paste 3 paragraphs you actually wrote.

Voiceprint makes 4 models rewrite one of them, then scores how much of your voice each one ate — which of your words died, which sentences doubled in length.

Leaves you a voice.md that stops it. Free, open source, nothing leaves your browser.
reasoning:
Voiceprint won because it is the only candidate where the output is simultaneously a diagnosis, a grievance people already voice loudly, and a thing worth posting. The others split: Fontsmith and Semantic If had the fresh-capability hook but no reason to share the result; One Sentence and Reviewed had audiences but well-known free incumbents; Clockskew and Directory Diff had presentation charm but no durable data behind them.

Three things decided it. First, the complaint is expressed, not latent — people already strip em dashes out of superstition, Wikipedia maintains a "Signs of AI writing" page, and Slate wrote about writers self-censoring. Second, the gap is real and I checked it twice: plenty of tools build you a voice card (Idiolect, unslop, Claude Styles) and plenty score text for slop, but nothing free puts four *named* models against your own paragraph and shows which one did the damage. Third, it ends with an artifact the person keeps and uses — voice.md pasted into their CLAUDE.md or their ChatGPT custom instructions — rather than a screenshot they discard.

It does not touch tonight's venture (Rightsline: ad-licence compliance for DTC creative ops) in audience, workflow or theme, and it is drawn from different material — the Caro interview's obsession with voice and the YC "LLMs That Write Well" signal, not the creator-marketing bookmark. It builds on no past library idea; the nearest neighbours, Skillscale and SkillPeek, serve agent developers inspecting repos, while this serves writers inspecting their own prose.

could_grow is true, with a caveat: the honest venture inside this is not the free tool but the measurement layer — a hosted style baseline that teams and publishers run on everything their writers and agents ship, to prove house voice survived. That is a real product. But it is explicitly not what gets built this weekend, and chasing it would ruin the project.

Score 7.8, dig_deeper. I held usefulness at 7 on purpose: the weekly board is a designed reason to return, not an observed one, and I have no evidence anyone comes back to a writing-diagnostic tool. That single number is the difference between this and a 9, and the validation test is aimed straight at it.
candidates_considered:
VENTURE
1. Rightsline — creator licence + platform-authorization clock joined to live ads in the brand's own Meta/TikTok accounts. PICK: named buyer, two clocks nobody watches, enforcement tooling already exists on the creator side but nothing on the brand side, and the first version is a read-only API join.
2. Micro-creator discovery for non-ecommerce buyers (clinics, gyms, local franchises) off the @shengkunye $0.002/creator pattern — dropped at screen: discovery is the most crowded corner of the category (Modash, Favikon, SARAL, Skeepers all priced $129-$599/mo) and the bookmark's own tool is open source and free.
3. Agentic TPM for non-software programs (construction, clinical trials) from @jakejooyoung's Serro — dropped at screen: Serro already sells the engineering case at $100/program, and the non-software version needs domain depth this builder does not have.
4. Client-visible agent work log for agencies, off DHH's Basecamp-for-Claude post — dropped at screen: Basecamp itself now ships agent participation with per-client visibility controls, and every PM tool is racing here.
5. Plaid-for-benefits wedge: document-chaser for nonprofit benefits navigators (YC RFS, Gustaf Alströmer) — dropped at screen: real pain and a real signal, but the buyer is grant-funded with 6-12 month procurement, which breaks this builder's "sellable in weeks" constraint.
6. AI-for-City-Hall wedge: plan-check correction triage — dropped before research as too close to the library's existing Backcheck (same permit coordinator, same correction-letter workflow).
7. Jev-style typed decision layer for insurance claim triage at MGAs — dropped at screen: the capability is new and cheap but the buyer is slow, regulated and needs a pilot year; also a thin wrapper on someone else's model.
8. Spark Ads / partnership code expiry monitor as a standalone free tool — not dropped, absorbed: this became the sharper half of the pick's wedge in round 1.
9. Data-centre supply-chain lead-time tracker for electrical contractors (YC RFS, Jared Friedman) — dropped at screen: no clean data source a solo builder can get, and the buyer is a procurement manager who buys via relationships.
10. Font/brand-asset licence auditor for design teams, off @nutlope's generated-fonts post — dropped at screen: real but tiny and episodic pain, no recurring budget, and it is the same rights-expiry shape as the pick with a much weaker buyer.

PROJECT
1. Fontsmith — prompt → a real TTF via DeepSeek V4.1 Flash SVG glyphs (from @nutlope's $0.02-per-font post). Dropped at screen: Mixfont, Lipi.ai and Creative Fabrica already ship prompt-to-TTF with downloads, and Perplexity confirmed the model emits SVG text that still needs assembly and hand-fixing — a weekend sunk into kerning, not a weekend shipping.
2. Voiceprint — paste your writing, four models rewrite it, see which ate your voice, get a voice.md. PICK.
3. Semantic If — a browser playground for Jev's typed Choice/Score decisions, write a natural-language condition and watch it fire with a calibrated probability. Finalist; lost. Real and cheap ($0.042/M in, output free, OAuth-able) but the audience is developers evaluating a classifier — the output is a probability bar, nothing anyone posts, and the awesome-jev-use-cases repo already hosts a browser demo.
4. Microcreator — find small creators with outsized engagement for your niche (from @shengkunye). Dropped at screen: depends on the open-source UGC discovery tool just announced in the bookmark itself; building on top of it is a thin wrapper, and it overlaps the creator/UGC audience of tonight's venture pick (Rightsline).
5. One Sentence — paste an essay or paste a book, get Caro's "what is this about, in one sentence" plus the sentences that earned it (from the Dwarkesh/Caro interview). Dropped at screen: summarisation is the single most commoditised LLM feature on earth; ChatGPT does it free in one line.
6. Reviewed — paste a diff and a PR description, get the Claude-Code-team-style "does this change match its stated intent" review (from @addyosmani). Dropped at screen: CodeRabbit, Greptile, PR-Agent, Kodus all occupy this, several free. No gap.
7. Clockskew — the three-clocks chart (models tick in days, GPUs in years, fabs in half-decades) as a live browsable timeline from public release dates (from @neimuc27, 3 likes). Dropped at screen: lovely as a presentation, but the dataset would be hand-assembled by me, which makes it an opinion piece, not a dataset.
8. Slackback — rebuild any app you screenshot as a clickable mock (from @mattyp's agents-rebuild-Slack-as-video post). Dropped: this is Napkins, which is in the builder's own taste file. Cloning an admired project is not a project.
9. Focusprint — an ADHD-shaped single-task shell over a coding agent (from @SavannahFeder's hyperfocus launch). Dropped: proposing a thin version of a product named in tonight's bookmarks, and a day's build cannot touch a real ADE.
10. Directory Diff — watch the Claude app directory (from @dhh's Basecamp launch) and post what appeared or vanished each week. Dropped at screen: too close to Deadlist, already in the library — same core workflow of checking whether listed things are still alive.
research_notes:
Venture: Reading pot (3/3): summarised Serro AI (agentic TPM, ~$100/program, $45/seat startup tier — enough to kill candidate 3), the Basecamp Claude connector (Basecamp already ships agents-alongside-clients with per-project visibility — killed candidate 4), and Jev by TypeSafe ($0.042/M input tokens, typed choice/score/boolean decisions, 70-500ms — shaped candidate 7 and later justified the cheap contract-clause classification in the pick). A fourth link, Addy Osmani's X article, could not be resolved by the tool and was not used.

Screening pot (6/6): influencer gifting/campaign tooling (crowded — killed candidate 2); government benefits income verification (real but slow-procurement buyer — killed candidate 5); nonprofit benefits navigators (grant-funded, no fast budget); agency client portals and AI reporting (saturated — killed candidate 4 conclusively); Jev typed-decision use cases including insurance triage (capability real, buyer slow); field-service/home-services dispatch (dominated by Connecteam, D365 Field Service, FieldCamp). Screening is what pushed me off the obvious creator-discovery read of the @shengkunye bookmark and onto the post-campaign rights step.

Deep research pot (12/12), on two finalists (Rightsline, and the creator-discovery-for-local-services idea which died early): established how rights are tracked today (manual spreadsheets, per-asset, rarely with expiry); that no major creator CRM or DAM joins a licence expiry to a live ad in the brand's ad account (Aspire's own docs say partnership ads have no expiry date; Brandfolder expiry only blocks DAM downloads; Bynder needs FADEL); found the creator-side enforcement market already productised and priced (Usage Hawk $24-$499/mo, ExpiredAds at 25% of recovery, now paused); confirmed Meta and TikTok APIs expose live ads, creative identifiers and — critically — a Spark Ads authorization end time, while Meta's public Ad Library API covers EU commercial ads via DSA Article 39 but not US-only commercial ads; priced the adjacent tools the buyer already pays for (Modash $299-$599, Atria $129-$959, Motion ~$750, Evisort ~$15k/yr estimate); and sized the workflow (10-30 creators/quarter, 20-50 creatives/month, 90d rights at +30-75% of base fee). The honest negative finding — no verifiable dataset of brands actually being invoiced for overruns — is why pain is 7.5 and not 9.

Sharpening pot (5/5): two calls on the Spark/partnership code expiry mechanism (confirmed no advance warning from TikTok, creator must extend before expiry, API exposes the end time) and the real cost of an outage (no defensible CPA-spike number — so I did not claim one); one on agency willingness to buy and resell a rights report (supportive, with the "it becomes admin" caveat now in riskiest_assumptions); one on who owns and signs at a $20-100M DTC brand ($300-1,000/mo sits inside a $200-$2,500/mo creator-software band); one on contract-extraction feasibility and enterprise pricing (Evisort ~$15k/yr, Ironclad/Luminance quote-only — confirming the empty middle).

Investor signals weighed: YC W27 "The $15-an-Hour Expert" (the ops manager becomes a rights administrator, used in why_now), "Plaid for Government Benefits" and "AI for City Hall" (both generated candidates; dropped for procurement speed and library overlap respectively), a16z "Prompt-free and proactive applications arrive" (the product never has a prompt box — it watches and intervenes) and "Startups tame the chaos of multimodal data" (contracts as PDFs, DM screenshots and emails). Signals aimed the search; the buyer and the gap came from my own research.
Sharpening (7.2 to 8.1): Round 1 — weak criterion: pain (6.5). The brand-side rights-overrun pain looked latent: Perplexity repeatedly reported industry guidance and plausible legal consequences but no verified cases of brands being invoiced, and no Reddit complaint corpus. Change to the idea: added the second clock — platform authorization expiry (TikTok Spark Ads codes, Instagram partnership codes) — and made the product a two-sided "rights clock" rather than a compliance register. Research (two sharpening calls): TikTok's own help docs confirm authorization expiry is an error state with no advance warning, creators can only extend *before* expiry, and an expired code requires a brand-new one; the API does expose an authorization end time, so the warning is buildable. The performance-loss call was honest in the other direction — no reliable "CPA spike" number exists and a short pause does not automatically reset Meta's learning phase — so I did not inflate the cost of an outage. Net: pain 6.5 → 7.5 (a real, self-interested, recurring operational failure, not a hypothetical legal one), wedge 8 → 8.5 (the delivery-outage alert is a single API field plus a date, sellable before the contract-parsing half is finished). Score before 7.2, after 8.1.

Round 2 — weak criterion: market_pull (7). Change: moved the first sale from the DTC brand's ops manager to the UGC/performance agency ops lead who covers 5-15 clients and already sells monthly reporting. Research: agencies do report monthly on creative output and some already package rights registries and takedown workflows (raasis.com), and creator-workflow tools already ship per-client unbranded exports — so a resellable report fits an existing motion. But the same call warned it becomes admin unless ingestion is near-zero, and no comparable category of resold rights-compliance reports exists. Evidence was supportive but not conclusive, so market_pull 7 → 7.5 only, and the agency-as-admin risk is now written into riskiest_assumptions.

Project: Reading pot (3 of 3): Perplexity on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 for font generation (confirmed it emits SVG text, not installable fonts — killed Fontsmith); Perplexity on Jev/TypeSafe (confirmed real, $0.042/M in, output free, Choice/Score/Noul types — kept Semantic If alive as a finalist); Perplexity on the @addyosmani article (identified it as the Claude Code team's code-review process, which seeded candidate 6).
Screening pot (5 of 5): one Google search each against the obvious killer. AI font generators → Mixfont, Lipi.ai, Creative Fabrica all ship prompt-to-TTF (Fontsmith dropped). Jev browser demos → awesome-jev-use-cases repo already has one. Calibrated-probability personal apps → only academic Brier-score literature, no consumer tool. AI code review → CodeRabbit, Greptile, PR-Agent, Kodus (Reviewed dropped). AI slop detectors → Taplio, slopdetector.org, dozens of unslop skills, which reframed the slop angle away from detection and toward per-model attribution.
Deep research pot (8 of 8): Perplexity on Jev's browser/CORS story and real per-item cost (~$0.026 per 1,000 classifications, but needs a proxy); Perplexity on existing voice-card tools (found Idiolect, Said My Way, Voice Analyzer, unslop — all produce cards, none attribute damage to a model); Perplexity on voice-loss measurement (found ScriptGrain's pairwise checker and deslopify, confirmed the multi-model side-by-side gap); Perplexity on the YC "LLMs That Write Well" claim (found the Nature Human Behaviour 21-50% variance result and flagged that the year-over-year-decline claim itself is unproven — so I cite the paper and not the decline); Perplexity on OpenRouter free models and DeepSeek pricing; Perplexity on multi-model rewrite playgrounds (Overchat, ZeroTwo, ChatPlayground exist, but none score style distance); Google on the Nature paper to confirm it is real and published Aug 2026; Google searches on handle-based voice tools and in-browser stylometry libraries, which pushed the design to deterministic in-browser metrics and away from an X-handle input (X data access is fragile and terms-restricted).
Sharpening pot (4 of 4): Perplexity on human-or-AI guessing games (found StyleMimic's Blind Test, which is the nearest share mechanic — informed the card design and warned me off a pure guessing-game framing); Perplexity on personal style-drift dashboards (found Coaching Stylist and Hold Your Voice, which killed the "track my own drift" return hook); Perplexity on OpenRouter OAuth PKCE and free-model rate limits (confirmed BYO-key from a static page, raised buildability to 8); Perplexity on whether any weekly crowd-voted board ranks models on preserving a user's voice (LMArena is generic, TextStyled and PersonalBench are static — confirmed the weekly board is fresh and kept it in).
Net effect: research killed two candidates outright, demoted one finalist, supplied the one genuinely new capability (cheap four-model fan-out on the visitor's own key), and replaced my first return-hook with one nobody else has built.
Sharpening (7.2 to 7.8): Round 1 — weakest criterion: usefulness (5, a one-time toy). The first version was "paste your writing, get a voice-loss score" — you run it once, you screenshot it, you leave. Change to the idea: the tool now ends on a generated voice.md with your real numbers and your real distinctive words, and a public weekly board of which model lost the most voice, refreshed Mondays. Research (Perplexity, sharpening pot) found Coaching Stylist and Hold Your Voice already do personal style-drift-over-time dashboards, so I dropped the "track my own drift weekly" version of the hook as not fresh, and kept the model-side board instead. A second check (Perplexity on LMArena creative-writing, TextStyled, PersonalBench) confirmed no public, regularly refreshed board ranks models on preserving a *user's* voice — LMArena is generic creative-writing preference, TextStyled and PersonalBench are static research benchmarks. Usefulness 5 → 7 (weekly board plus a durable artifact, but no evidence yet anyone returns, so capped). Wow 7 → 8: the per-model attribution plus the diff of your dead words is the unexpected part, not the score.
Round 2 — weakest remaining: buildability (7, unknowns around calling four models from a static page). Change: the fan-out runs on the visitor's own OpenRouter key via OAuth PKCE, with a demo mode of pre-baked samples so the value lands before any auth; all scoring is deterministic in-browser JS, no LLM judge. Research confirmed OpenRouter supports OAuth PKCE from a static page for exactly this (openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/auth/oauth), that free models exist at 20 req/min and 50/day, and that DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is ~$0.031/M in and $0.27/M out — fractions of a cent per bake-off. Buildability 7 → 8 (every dependency checked and cheap; not 9 because the OAuth round-trip plus canvas card is more than a static page with zero moving parts). Freshness held at 8 and not raised: the Nature paper (Aug 2026) and the YC RFS are recent and confirmed, but a determined person could have built a cruder version a year ago.
prototype_summary: Voiceprint is a four-screen interactive prototype that measures a writer's voiceprint from pasted text, runs a simulated bake-off where four AI models rewrite a paragraph with word-level green/red diff highlighting showing voice loss percentages, and generates a copyable voice.md style guide plus a shareable result card.
